The '''1959 DDR-Oberliga''' was the eleventh season of the [[DDR-Oberliga]], the first tier of [[East German football league system|league football]] in [[East Germany]]. Rather than in the traditional autumn-spring format the Oberliga played for six seasons from 1955 to 1960 in the calendar year format, modelled on the system used in the [[Soviet Union]]. From 1961–62 onwards the league returned to its traditional format.

The league was contested by fourteen teams. [[FC Erzgebirge Aue|SC Wismut Karl-Marx-Stadt]], incidentally based at [[Aue, Saxony|Aue]] and not [[Chemnitz|Karl-Marx-Stadt]], won the championship, the club's last of three national East German championships.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesd/ddrchamp.html |title= East Germany - List of Champions |website= [[RSSSF]] |access-date= 19 January 2016}}</ref><ref name="Meister" >{{cite web |url=https://www.dfb.de/historie/ddr-fussball/meister/ |title= DDR-Meister |website=dfb.de |publisher=[[German Football Association]] |access-date= 19 January 2016|language=de|trans-title= East German champions}}</ref> On the strength of the 1959 title Wismut qualified for the [[1960–61 European Cup]] where the club was knocked out by [[SK Rapid Wien]] in the first round. League runners-up [[FC Viktoria Frankfurt|ASK Vorwärts Berlin]] qualified for the [[1960–61 European Cup Winners' Cup]] instead of [[FDGB-Pokal]] winner [[BFC Dynamo|SC Dynamo Berlin]] and was knocked out by [[Rudá Hvězda Brno]] in the preliminary round.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/ec/ec196061.html |title= European Competitions 1960-61|website= [[RSSSF]] |access-date= 19 January 2016}}</ref>

[[Bernd Bauchspieß]] of [[Chemie Zeitz]] was the league's top scorer with 18 goals.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.weltfussball.de/torschuetzenkoenige/gdr-oberliga/ |title= DDDR » Oberliga » Torschützenkönige  |website= Weltfussball.de |access-date= 19 January 2016|language=de|trans-title=DDR-Oberliga top scorers }}</ref>

==Table==
